system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer position:** Do not accept the package as drafted. The targets below are proposed negotiating positions, not existing agreements or mandatory legal requirements. Assessment is based on the supplied documents, not independent review of DD-002–DD-012.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Open at **50% / AUD 12m** for general warranties, with separate treatment for protected categories below. | **Counter:** 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer; assess any concession alongside security, insurance and other limitations. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower de minimis, e.g. **AUD 10,000**; **AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, recovering qualifying claims from dollar one once exceeded; aggregate related claims. | **Counter:** The proposed thresholds compound the cap and could exclude numerous economically significant claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranty notice within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24–36 months** for general warranties only; reasonable notice requirements, preservation of contingent claims and no unduly short proceedings deadline. | **Amend:** Allow sufficient reporting cycles to identify problems and prevent general deadlines cutting down other remedies. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limits. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, authority, ownership, all issued shares and freedom from encumbrances; **100% price cap**, no thresholds and a longer survival period, opening at **seven years**. | **Reject common regime:** Ownership and authority are core acquisition risks, not ordinary business warranty risks. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express preservation of claims for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment, outside contractual caps, thresholds, time bars and remedy restrictions; address attribution expressly. | **Require overriding carve-out:** The Seller must not use contractual protections to shelter its fraud or fraud attributable to it. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the indexed data room, accounts, registers and public corporate records, including matters merely “referred to”. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; specific warranty cross-references and a frozen, identifiable disclosure bundle. | **Reject blanket disclosure:** A document dump or reference to another source should not transfer unidentified risks to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for matters known to the Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the qualifier; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without constructive/imputed knowledge or investigation duties. | **Delete or narrowly confine:** Access to information is not equivalent to knowing a warranty is untrue or accepting its consequences. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, although no final consent or evidence of satisfaction of associated conditions is supplied. | Buyer-benefit completion condition requiring effective written consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions, without materially adverse changes; Buyer-controlled waiver and long-stop termination rights. | **Require substantive satisfaction before Completion:** A document alone may not preserve a customer representing approximately **30% of FY26 revenue**. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout figure covering interest and fees; repayment through Completion funds flow, reducing Seller proceeds; effective releases of all relevant security and guarantees at Completion. | **Reject unsecured post-Completion release:** Debt-free/cash-free pricing requires actual debt discharge and an enforceable release mechanism at closing. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses are omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable employer on-costs through a deduction, payment or adequately funded retention; confirm conditions and avoid double counting. | **Itemise and allocate expressly:** A statement that bonuses are the Seller’s matter does not stop the acquired Company bearing the liability. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, without independent proof of non-payment or a confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment status and satisfaction of transfer conditions; effective assignment/confirmation of necessary IP rights before Completion, plus a standalone indemnity covering ownership defects, claims, remediation and reasonable defence costs. | **Broaden protection and require evidence:** Paying an invoice alone may not establish complete, usable IP title or cover downstream losses. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational issue said unlikely to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, access to findings, containment and legally required notifications; interim covenants and a specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident liabilities, with retention considered once exposure is assessed. | **Keep open pending investigation:** The evidence establishes neither a confirmed notifiable breach nor a basis to dismiss the risk. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** commitment, timing, commercial purpose, termination rights and accrual status; require consent if outside agreed conduct thresholds and allocate any debt-like or transaction-driven amount expressly. | **Reserve classification and aggregate related commitments:** Neither automatic Seller liability nor ordinary-course treatment is established by the supplied facts. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend across all Claims unless excluded. | Express, overriding category rules for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, price/debt adjustments, covenants and fraud; clearly specify each applicable cap and deadline. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture:** Otherwise broad “all Claims” wording can silently neutralise separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s register showing Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Verify register, issuance and transfer history, beneficial ownership, share classes, options/conversion rights and encumbrances; obtain executed transfers, certificates or appropriate replacements, approvals and updated register at Completion. | **Verify independently and require completion deliverables:** The register is evidence, not a complete assurance of unencumbered ownership and fully diluted control. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Treats tax and IP warranties as settled under the general regime. | Keep both expressly open: separate pre-Completion tax indemnity/deed, tax warranties and claims procedures; enhanced IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection. Open at price-level caps, tax survival through relevant assessment periods plus a buffer, and a longer IP period, e.g. six years. | **Reject deemed settlement:** Tax can emerge late and IP underpins business value; neither should default to the 20% cap and 18-month deadline. |

**Implementation priority:** Make the category exclusions override clauses **9.3, 12.8 and 20.5**, and ensure disclosure or Buyer knowledge cannot defeat specific indemnities, payment obligations or completion conditions unless expressly agreed.
=== END ADVICE ===
